sprint_goal: Maya's ledger and signed runs keep what was decided, and her gates say up front what they need and cost.

seats.achievable: yes - the regrooming closes round 1's engineering risks. The flag is now --ruling, so it no longer clashes with supersede's --authorised-by. The check lives in round_refusal for every verdict writer (BG1003 AC3). BG1025 AC3 judges the principal by sign's own rule. BG0950, BG0976, BG0978, BG0944 and BG0945 now declare their changelog fragments, and BG0950 also declares test_critic.py. Every unit maps to a clause. The ledger: BG1003, BG0950, BG0944 AC1 and AC2. Signed runs: BG1025, BG0944 AC3, BG0945. What the gates need: US1003, US1004, US1005, BG0976, BG0978. What they cost: US1006. 24 points, and the build order still honours every Depends on.
seats.done_means: All 31 criteria across the 11 units are green under verify_ac. critic.py record --ruling D0352 records BG0993's round 3 and --ruling D0353 its round 4, after which BG0993 reaches Fixed under D0354. Record refuses a ruling that is absent, not accepted or unrelated, naming which, and every delivery-verdict writer gets the same answer from round_refusal. sprint sign leaves a carried Open bug Open, names it as carried, moves every other unit, and the signed page still checks VALID. A sealed unit's status changes through transition only with --principal and --reason, and never with the unit's author or a reviewer as principal. A reviewer's verdict in the contract's shape, semicolons in its evidence included, records unedited, with each blocking finding once. enable-hooks.sh and the pre-push preflight name what the gate needs before the gate runs. The cost line cites only this clone's own measurements. The existing hook fixtures pass unchanged apart from the cost-line test US1006 rewrites.
seats.one_increment: no - the rewording does not change the code. The critic, sprint/transition and pre-push clusters share no file and no dependency, and they can build as parallel tracks. The amended goal now names both halves honestly, so every unit sits under it, but the close should report two increments delivered, not one.
seats.note: The regrooming leaves two build points open. First, BG1003 should say what 'names the unit' reads. The id appearing in the decision's text is what can be built. Each ruling should also authorise one round only: D0352 and D0353 each grant exactly one, but AC2 does not refuse a second past-cap round under a ruling already recorded on an earlier row, so a single ruling would lift the cap on that unit for good. And D0354 mentions BG0989 and BG0994 as well as BG0993, so a text match would accept it for either of those units, though it authorises no round. Second, BG0950 at 2 points now changes the split rule, the BLOCKING fold and the pins in test_critic.py; it should keep the existing `\;` escape working for --issues callers. The pre-push cluster still builds strictly in the listed order.

seats.achievable: yes - the oracles round 1 called weak are now executable. BG0945 runs its Steps through the CLI (LC-018). BG0950 AC3 is a single requirement, and AC1's two-finding block catches a build that stops splitting altogether. BG1025 AC1 re-checks that the signed page is still VALID (LC-016), and AC3 now has four negatives: no principal, no reason, the unit's author, and a recorded reviewer. 'Up front' is exactly what US1005's test proves (the stub gate.py is never invoked), so the goal no longer claims a time that no AC measures. Three oracles could still go green on a broken build; they are in the note.
seats.done_means: verify_ac is green on all 31 criteria, each from a test that fails on its named mutant, and the following also hold. BG1003 refuses a second past-cap round under a ruling already recorded on an earlier row for that unit. BG0976's tests control what ssh -G returns rather than reading the machine's own ssh config. US1006's no-fixed-figure tests refuse any number with a time unit, not only the two restored literals. BG0944's three pins each fail on their named mutant in a scratch copy.
seats.one_increment: no - two test surfaces with no shared fixture: the skill's scripts/tests (critic, sprint, transition) and tools/tests (the hook chain). The amended goal names both, so every criterion traces to a clause, but the done bar is still the sum of two.
seats.note: BG0976: isolating HOME does not cover ssh. OpenSSH reads ~/.ssh/config from the passwd entry's home directory, not from $HOME, and it reads /etc/ssh/ssh_config regardless. So if the fix calls ssh -G as proposed, then on a machine whose own ssh config sets ServerAliveInterval, AC2 (the warning prints when none is set) goes red; on a machine without one, AC1 can pass for the wrong reason. A stub `ssh` on the fixture PATH, or -F pointing at a fixture config, lets the test decide the answer. BG1003 AC2 lists no case for a ruling already spent on an earlier round, which is the case that lets the cap lapse. US1006 AC1 says the cost line 'states no fixed number of minutes': the test should reject any figure with a time unit, or a reworded '5 min' or '300 seconds' passes.
